subject: Exercise: inference routing component — handoff, deadline & review plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang+ri@example.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exercise: inference routing component — handoff, deadline & review plan

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for interviewing with Redwood Inference — enjoyed our conversation last week. As discussed, attached is the exercise prompt that we use for backend/infra candidates: a short, open-ended implementation + writeup focused on designing a routing layer for model variants.

Quick summary/expectations:
- Deliverables: a short README (design decisions + tradeoffs), runnable reference (Docker or single archive), and a small correctness/perf note.
- Deadline: 48 hours from receipt — please submit by Mon Aug 9, 11:59 PM PT. If you need an extension, tell us before Aug 8 and we can accommodate.
- Submission method: reply to this thread with a link to a public or private repo (OK to provide a link with read access), or attach a zip.
- Allowed resources: public packages and docs are fine; we do not expect or require access to internal Redwood code or datasets. See attached FAQ in the PDF.

Attachments: exercise-instructions.pdf (prompt, checklist, example scoring rubric)

Next steps on our side: Markus will coordinate reviewers; we’re tentatively scheduling a 45-minute debrief on Tue Aug 10 for the hiring panel. I’ll add a calendar placeholder and confirm once we have reviewers assigned.

If anything is unclear, reply here or ping Monica. Good luck!

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Engineering Manager, Recruiting Partner
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang+ri@example.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exercise: inference routing component — handoff, deadline & review plan

Hi Neha — thanks for sending and for the clarity. I have a quick question: for the perf notes, is it okay to run lightweight synthetic benchmarks (locally) and include those results? Also — are we allowed to use any hosted vector store or should I keep everything local?

I’ll get started and aim for the deadline.

Best,
Emily

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang+ri@example.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exercise: inference routing component — handoff, deadline & review plan

Hi Emily — great questions. Short answers:
- Synthetic/local microbenchmarks are perfect; point out the machine you ran them on and any limitations in the README.
- You can use hosted tools (e.g., managed vector DBs) if it helps, but please note any free tiers used and include a short note on reproducibility. We don’t need production-scale data.

Also, a note for transparency: our reviewers will look for clarity of tradeoffs, correctness of the design, and a runnable artifact. If you prefer to submit a private GitHub link, include collaborator access for neha.kapoor@redwood.ai; otherwise attach a zip in the reply.

I’ve added a tentative calendar placeholder for Tue Aug 10 09:30–10:15 PT for the debrief — final time to follow once reviewers confirm.

— Neha

I’ve attached a short review checklist to keep scoring consistent (review-checklist.md). We’ll meet Tue Aug 10 09:30–10:15 PT to sync and make hiring recommendation. If anyone cannot make it, flag immediately so Monica can find an alternate.
